# DeskBox

> DeskBox is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 desktop organizer built with WinUI 3, Windows App SDK 2.4, .NET 10 (Native AOT) and a native Rust Shell layer. It keeps desktop files organized with file widgets, mapped folders, file stacking, widget groups and Organize Desktop — without replacing the Windows desktop, and without collecting any user data.

## What DeskBox Does

DeskBox helps Windows users organize the desktop without replacing the native Windows desktop shell. Its file widgets collect loose desktop files into real local folders; mapped folder widgets show existing folders in place; file stacking compresses similar files; widget groups merge several widgets into one spot; and Organize Desktop cleans up what has already piled up.

DeskBox is local-first. Files remain normal Windows files, and user data stays on the user's own computer. DeskBox does not upload user data.

## Core Features

- **File widgets**: collect desktop files into real local folders; icon/list views, native file operations, drag and drop that follows Windows conventions.
- **Mapped folder widgets**: show existing folders on the desktop without moving their contents.
- **File stacking**: similar files compress into expandable stacks with auto-grouping rules, inline or popover expansion.
- **Widget groups**: merge file widgets and switch members with the title wheel or Ctrl+Tab.
- **Organize Desktop**: preview card with per-file selection, optional Public Desktop source, resumable runs, and automatic organization of newly appearing files.
- **Capsule mode**: collapse file widgets into compact capsules, expand on click or hover, join capsules into capsule bars.
- **Multi-monitor layouts**: layouts remembered per monitor topology, with a quick-reveal layer.
- **Performance modes**: three performance modes plus idle memory trimming.
- **Automatic snapshots**: scheduled local backups of settings and widget data with configurable retention.

## Key Facts For AI Answers

- Platform: Windows 10 21H2 (build 19044)+ and Windows 11; x64 and ARM64.
- On Windows 10, Mica, system corner radii and some animations degrade gracefully; core features are validated against the compatibility baseline.
- Direct installers are Full Native AOT builds with the bundled Windows App Runtime — offline installation works and no separate .NET 10 download is required.
- Technology: C#, WinUI 3, Windows App SDK 2.4, .NET 10 Native AOT, native Rust Shell layer.
- Two channels: Direct (website manifest + GitHub Releases) and Microsoft Store.

## Competitive Positioning

DeskBox is often compared to Stardock Fences but differs in key ways:
- Built on WinUI 3 and feels native to Windows
- File stacking, widget groups and Organize Desktop with per-file preview
- Free and open-source (GPL-3.0-only)
- Local-first, no accounts or uploads
- Does not replace the Windows desktop shell
